CHROMIUM: Input: atmel_mxt_ts - defer probe if reset GPIO is busy We like to source different touch panels, but connect them to the same regulators/GPIOs. If they are both probed at the same time one is loses with -EBUSY. We can't sequence probes in any meaningful way since from the driver core and i2c core these are 2 completely separate devices residing at different addresses. Let's convert -EBUSY from GPIO to -EPROBE_DEFER so that the loser gets another chance (the drawback is that loser that does not actually have corresponding device might be retrying probing for quite a few times - but I do not see any easy way of fixing this). This is not upstreamable IMO. BUG=chrome-os-partner:39123 TEST=Build and boot on Minnie. Change-Id: I797e017e488990dd18cf3bf50346fce45212784f Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/266225 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit a8c1c53f3bf0acc635eba9df87022f568ef01d25) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/414930 Tested-by: Jongpil Jung <jongpil19.jung@samsung.com> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Input: atmel_mxt_ts - implement power up procedure for S2R On some ARM systems kernel should control power rails to which the touchpad or touchscreen is attached. Previously we only executed proper power-up sequence at boot time and expected to regulators to stay powered on suring S2R. This change adds proper power down/power up sequence to the suspend and resume handlers in the driver and allows us to turn regulators off and on during system sleep transitions. Additionally we ensure that inhibit/uninhibit and open/close to not clash with each other with regard to controller power state and that we keep the device in low powered mode while it is closed (or inhibited). Note that even device is closed or inhibited we still keep power rails on to allow sysfs access (for example for config or firmware flashing). BUG=chrome-os-partner:38094,chrome-os-partner:38175 TEST=powerd_dbus_suspend, then wakeup system, verify devices work normally; execute similar test with closing/opening the lid; also exercise "inhibit" interface. Execute tests on devices that have either Atmel touchscreen or touchpad or both. Change-Id: I1663eb486089b80835bcfecc717ee04e1dead69a Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/275668 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit b08ba72f5c0addf4a027fc34f4ae7fc166f2f6ff) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/414932 Tested-by: Jongpil Jung <jongpil19.jung@samsung.com> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: Input: atmel_mxt_ts - ensure we are in deep sleep when disabling T100 Atmel's firmware gets confused if we do not have T15 and try to disable T100 while controller is not in deep sleep. They also say that when disabling T100 we should also disable T101 (hover) and T104 (Aux touch config), otherwise they consider the configuration invalid. While they will look into making the firmware more robust, let's stop disabling T100 in mxt_stop() - Atmel says that it does not result in additional power savings compared to the deep sleep. Also, in mxt_start(), read current value of T100 control register and avoid writing it unless it is different from what we want it to be, and do it before we bring the device out of deep sleep mode. BUG=chrome-os-partner:57704, chrome-os-partner:59131 TEST=Built and booted Celes, used touchscreen Change-Id: Ie47a90a6e9a5bc9ff71e200027abfdc2e55e8716 Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/414933 Tested-by: Jongpil Jung <jongpil19.jung@samsung.com> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: config: disable Synaptics I2C driver This driver only supports Synaptics I2C touchpad controller on eXeda mobile device. It only works in relative mode and thus is not compatible with Xorg Synaptics driver, so it it no use for us. It was disabled on !X86, now let's disable it everywhere. CHROMIUM: config: disable PS/2 protocol extensions on X86 We are no longer using PS/2 trackpads and we do not have externals PS/2 ports, so the only potential user of PS/2 device is amd64-generic under QEMU. So let's disable extended protocols to save memory (users building custom images can re-enable what they need). BUG=None TEST=Build and boot several devices Change-Id: I8b47859798c7a28d1ff70346b96154978ccaf1e6 Signed-off-by: Dmitry Torokhov <dtor@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/415440 Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Benson Leung <bleung@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: tpm: cr50: Start TPM on resume from suspend-to-idle If using suspend-to-idle (S0ix) then the BIOS is not executed on resume, but the TPM may go into a deep sleep state and lose context, so it needs to be told to start up and restore that saved state. However the TPM does not immediately go into a deep sleep state, so if we wake up too early it may not have lost state and will return a code indicating it is already initialized. In order to prevent this from generating a confusing error message in syslog the command is done without a failure string, and the non-fatal return code is filtered out. BUG=chrome-os-partner:59895 TEST=manual: 1) Test S3 suspend-to-ram to ensure it functions as usual with no changes. 2) Test S0ix suspend-to-idle with a long residency in suspend, and check that the TPM context is restored when the system wakes. 3) Test S0ix suspend-to-idle with a short residency in suspend, and ensure that there are no error messages in syslog after wake. Change-Id: Ic8ba712b18afb7ea87b68fe7d35f07f6a508ece2 Signed-off-by: Duncan Laurie <dlaurie@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/415535 Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Furquan Shaikh <furquan@chromium.org>
